key_insight: An AI model’s public name can stay the same even when the model or its integrations change. The paper argues that meaningful versioning is essential for scientific reproducibility and regulatory oversight.
problem_solved: Updates made without corresponding identifier changes make it difficult to establish which AI system was tested, deployed, or reviewed.
method: Identify the mismatch between changing AI systems and unchanged public identifiers.
Examine how this mismatch undermines reproducibility and regulatory oversight.
Argue for versioning practices that meet the needs of researchers and regulators.
impact: Meaningful version identifiers could help practitioners track changes, reproduce evaluations, and document which system was assessed. This would make AI development and deployment more accountable.
visual_elements: A timeline showing multiple AI updates beneath one unchanged public model name.
A before-and-after diagram contrasting ambiguous identifiers with distinct version labels.
A model-and-integrations diagram highlighting that changes extend beyond the model itself.
Research and regulatory icons linked to a shared version identifier.
paper_authors: Vasilios Mavroudis, Dan Ristea, Lauritz Morlock, Carlos Mougan
